title: Juniper and the Songbook
premise: Sebastian Reyes, a pastry chef drowning in debt, inherits half of her late grandmother's stubborn apple orchard alongside Juniper Hale, the childhood friend she abandoned ten years ago after a betrayal neither has named. Forced to share the orchard through one harvest season to satisfy the deed's terms, they rebuild trust over cider presses, night markets, and a battered family songbook whose melodies hold the truth of what really happened that last summer. At the orchard's harvest festival, Sebastian finally speaks the rehearsed apology she has carried for a decade, saving both the orchard and the love she thought was lost.
about_author: Ivo Thackeray is the pen name of a former line cook who spent six seasons in small-town kitchens before turning to fiction. Their writing blends food, folklore, and the quiet geography of second chances.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Her café teeters on foreclosure as a lawyer's letter arrives: she has inherited half of Wren Hollow Orchard — jointly, with a stranger's name beside hers. The emotional beat is dread laced with desperate hope; an inheritance might save the café, but the deed's terms demand she live and work the land through harvest.

chapters.title: The Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper, a music restorer, receives the same letter and recognizes Sebastian's name with a cold, old anger. She drives to the orchard intending to sell her half immediately, only to find the deed forbids sale until the festival ends. The beat: reluctant arrival, armor firmly on.

chapters.title: Terms of the Deed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The two meet at the orchard house, all clipped politeness and unfinished sentences. Reading the deed aloud, they learn the harvest-work clause. Sebastian proposes a truce: sixty days, then part forever. The beat is brittle negotiation masking grief neither will voice.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. First weeks of shared labor: pruning, grafting, awkward proximity. Sebastian finds the old songbook in the attic — their grandmother's handwritten tunes, some in Juniper's teenage handwriting. Guilt sharpens. Beat: tenderness sneaking past defenses through work and memory.

chapters.title: Cider and Confessions Adjacent
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A storm forces them into the cider barn overnight; near-confessions circle but never land. Juniper reveals fragments of her decade since — the conservatory, the silence — while pointedly avoiding the summer everything broke. Beat: warmth kindling against both their intentions.

chapters.title: The Songbook's Missing Pages
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They discover pages torn from the songbook — including the song written the summer of the betrayal. Sebastian realizes Juniper believes Sebastian stole credit for their shared composition years ago. Misunderstanding crystallizes into open accusation. Beat: rising tension, the wound reopened.

chapters.title: Market Day, Broken Things
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A joint stall at the town market nearly succeeds — until a rival buyer exploits the rift, and a public argument exposes their conflict. The café's bank calls with final notice; selling her half would solve everything but break the deed. Beat: rock bottom, pride and panic colliding.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Last Verse
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Searching the orchard house for the missing pages, Juniper finds grandmother's letter: it was grandmother who submitted the song under Sebastian's name, believing she was protecting them both from a predatory publisher. The betrayal was never Sebastian's. Beat: devastating reversal, grief transmuting into longing.

chapters.title: The Festival Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On festival eve, with the deed's deadline hours away, Sebastian rehearses the sentence she has carried for ten years — and loses her nerve when Juniper announces she'll sign the sale papers at dawn. The torn pages are found tucked in the piano bench. Beat: climax pressure, everything hanging on words unspoken.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Sung
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. Before the whole festival crowd, Sebastian says the rehearsed apology aloud, then plays the restored song from the mended songbook. Juniper tears up the sale papers. Epilogue-flavored close: the café moves into the orchard house, the orchard thrives, and the songbook gains a new verse in two hands. Beat: catharsis, belonging, home.
